141.solution: Taking 1 mm as the slit separation, the shift is \(\dfrac{(\mu - 1)tD}{d} = \dfrac{0.5 \times 0.06 \times 10^{-3} \times 2}{10^{-3}} = 0.06\) m \(= 6\) cm (independent of the wavelength).

142.solution: A quarter of a fringe width is a phase difference of \(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\), where \(I = I_0\cos^2\dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{I_0}{2}\). The ratio is 2.

143.solution: Path \(\dfrac{\lambda}{6}\) is a phase of \(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\), so \(\dfrac{I}{I_0} = \cos^2\dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{3}{4} = 0.75\).

144.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
144.subtopic: de Broglie Wavelength and Matter Waves
144.solution: Absorbed light transfers momentum \(\dfrac{P}{c}\) per second and reflected light \(\dfrac{2P}{c}\): \(F = \dfrac{(0.4 + 2 \times 0.6) \times 60}{3 \times 10^8} = \dfrac{96}{3 \times 10^8} = 3.2 \times 10^{-7}\) N.

148.subtopic: Transistors — BJT, CE Amplifier, and Gain
148.solution: Voltage gain \(= \beta\dfrac{R_o}{R_i} = 50 \times 2.5 = 125\), so the output peak is \(125 \times 10\) mV \(= 1.25\) V.

149.subtopic: Transistors — BJT, CE Amplifier, and Gain
149.solution: In an n-p-n transistor the base is p-type and both emitter and collector are n-type, so each diode has its anode (p side) at the base: both diodes point away from B, one towards E and one towards C. That is circuit B.

150.subtopic: Band Theory, Doping, and Semiconductor Types
150.solution: In a good conductor the valence and conduction bands overlap, so electrons move freely without leaving holes in a filled band.
